# Zaaheen

> Zaaheen keeps what your AI assistants know about you on your own computer, encrypted, and entirely under your control.

Zaaheen is a desktop app that gives AI assistants one private, persistent memory about the person using them. Memories are stored and encrypted on that person's own computer and are never uploaded. The account is only for signing in and the subscription; it never holds the memories.

- Current version: 0.3.9, for 64-bit Windows (tested on Windows 11) and for Macs with an Apple chip (M1 or newer) (tested on macOS 26).
- Download: Windows https://dl.zaaheen.com/Zaaheen_0.3.9_x64.msi (150 MB, SHA-256 8e79d08b6275c4b82e92370c19e840f44ab5475039df229394211e0c7e24f29f); Mac https://dl.zaaheen.com/Zaaheen_0.3.9_aarch64.dmg (156 MB, SHA-256 b502087a94d80b42b90a9ac71742a2cbea576150cce301f24e61e926ea78699b), a disk image: drag Zaaheen into Applications and open it from there.
- Can't find Applications on a Mac? Open Finder (the blue and white face at the left of the Dock) and choose Applications in the sidebar on the left. Or, with Finder open, press Shift-Command-A.
- Free trial: 30 days, no card needed.
- Price after the trial: $5 a month or $48 a year (US dollars, plus VAT or sales tax where it applies). Both plans include everything. Sold through our reseller Paddle.com.
- Cancel any time in the app: Settings, then Account, then "Cancel subscription". A payment is refunded in full if asked within 14 days of it, once per person.
- Tested with: Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity. Other apps that support MCP should work the same way.
- Delete everything: one button destroys the encryption key and the files, leaving what remains on disk unreadable.
- Public code: the source is published at https://github.com/shahbaz242630/zaaheen so anyone can read how memories are encrypted and check that nothing sends them anywhere. It is for reading and security review, not open source: the licence does not allow running or sharing your own version.
- Linux and phones: not available yet.

## What Zaaheen gives a connected AI app

Zaaheen runs a local MCP server with six tools:

- memory_read: the main tool. Ask one question in plain words and get the matching facts about the person, or a clear "nothing stored" answer.
- memory_search: browse stored memories by free text, best matches first.
- memory_write: save one fact about the person, into one of their areas.
- memory_update: replace a stored memory with a corrected one.
- memory_delete: forget a memory, when the person asks.
- memory_help: the person's areas (names, labels, how many memories each holds) and the full guide to Zaaheen: areas, adding memories, undo, the hourly limit, connecting apps and what to do when something seems missing. Use it instead of guessing how the app works.

## Areas

- Memories are kept in areas; the Zaaheen app calls them boundaries (its Boundaries tab). Every memory is in exactly one area.
- A connected AI app can read and save in every area the person has, including an area created after the app connected.
- Two areas always exist: default (what the person adds in the app unless they choose another area) and personal (where AI apps save when the person does not name an area).
- Save into personal unless the person names an area; then use its exact name (capitals included).
- Only the person creates areas, in the Zaaheen app (Boundaries, then "+ New boundary"). Saving into an area that does not exist saves nothing and answers with the person's areas and the steps. Never tell the person something does not exist: call memory_help, which has the areas and the full guide.

- Undo: a memory deleted or replaced through memory_delete or memory_update waits for 30 days in the Zaaheen app, under Memories, then "Recently deleted", where the person can restore it. AI apps cannot open or empty that list.
- Limit: all connected AI apps together can delete or change at most 30 memories an hour. Past that, the tools answer that Zaaheen has paused deletes and edits; tell the person they can delete or edit in the Zaaheen app, or try again within the hour.

## Helping someone connect Zaaheen

- First, the person opens Zaaheen on their computer and signs in; the first sign-in from the app starts the free trial.
- In Zaaheen: the Agents tab, then "Connect an app", then the app. That tab shows the exact setting for their computer (its own install path), ready to copy: prefer it to the usual paths below (Windows C:\Program Files\Zaaheen\zaaheen.exe, Mac /Applications/Zaaheen.app/Contents/MacOS/zaaheen). Use the Copy buttons; a space typed before the command stops it working.
- Codex (terminal) and ChatGPT Desktop share one settings file (.codex/config.toml); the Cursor IDE uses Cursor Desktop's settings. Connect once.
- Other apps: https://zaaheen.com/docs/connect-other-apps/. More fixes: https://zaaheen.com/docs/troubleshooting/.

### Claude Desktop

Please follow all 3 steps. If you skip one, Claude Desktop may not use Zaaheen.
- Step 1A: The quick way: in Zaaheen, Agents, "Connect an app", "Claude Desktop", then "Save the extension". Zaaheen saves a small Claude extension, and Claude asks you to install it. Zaaheen saved the extension to your Downloads folder. In Claude, open Settings, then Extensions, then Advanced settings, then Install Extension, and choose "Zaaheen for Claude.mcpb".
- Step 1B: Or add it yourself (Windows): In Claude, open Settings, then Developer, then Edit Config. Add this to the file it shows you, save it, then quit Claude and open it again: { "mcpServers": { "zaaheen": { "command": "C:\\Program Files\\Zaaheen\\zaaheen.exe", "args": ["mcp", "serve"] } } }
- Step 1B: Or add it yourself (Mac): In Claude, open Settings, then Developer, then Edit Config. Add this to the file it shows you, save it, then quit Claude and open it again: { "mcpServers": { "zaaheen": { "command": "/Applications/Zaaheen.app/Contents/MacOS/zaaheen", "args": ["mcp", "serve"] } } }
- Step 2: Check it's connected: In Claude, open Settings, then Extensions. Zaaheen is listed there and switched on. If you added it yourself (Step 1B), it is listed under Settings, then Developer, instead.
- Step 3: Tell Claude Desktop to use Zaaheen (don't skip this): Claude looks in its own memory first. In Claude, open Settings, then Account, and add this line under Instructions for Claude: "When I ask you to remember something, save it in Zaaheen. Before answering anything about me, my preferences, my work or my plans, also check my Zaaheen memory, even when your own memory has nothing."
- Guide: https://zaaheen.com/docs/connect-claude/

### Cursor Desktop

Please follow both steps. If you skip one, Cursor Desktop may not use Zaaheen.
Using the Cursor IDE? Connect Zaaheen here, through Cursor Desktop: the IDE has no MCP settings of its own, and it uses the ones you set in Cursor Desktop, so connecting once is enough for both.
- Step 1A: The quick way: in Zaaheen, Agents, "Connect an app", "Cursor Desktop", then "Connect it for me". Zaaheen opens Cursor, and Cursor asks you to install Zaaheen. It can take up to a minute for Cursor to open and show its Install box, so please wait for it, then click Install. Cursor should now be showing its Install box. Click Install, and it's connected. If nothing has appeared, switch to the Cursor window: the box may be behind this one.
- Step 1B: Or add it yourself (Windows): In Cursor Desktop, choose Customize in the left bar, then MCPs. Scroll to the bottom, choose + New MCP server, and paste this in. Save it: { "mcpServers": { "zaaheen": { "command": "C:\\Program Files\\Zaaheen\\zaaheen.exe", "args": ["mcp", "serve"] } } }
- Step 1B: Or add it yourself (Mac): In Cursor Desktop, choose Customize in the left bar, then MCPs. Scroll to the bottom, choose + New MCP server, and paste this in. Save it: { "mcpServers": { "zaaheen": { "command": "/Applications/Zaaheen.app/Contents/MacOS/zaaheen", "args": ["mcp", "serve"] } } }
- Step 2: Check it's connected: In Cursor Desktop, choose Customize in the left bar, then MCPs. zaaheen is listed there and connected.
- Guide: https://zaaheen.com/docs/connect-cursor/

### ChatGPT Desktop

Please follow all 3 steps. If you skip one, ChatGPT Desktop may not use Zaaheen.
- Step 1: Add it yourself (Windows): 1. In ChatGPT Desktop, open Settings, then Plugins at the top, and choose MCP. Open the drop-down in the top right corner and choose Add MCP server. 2. Name: Zaaheen 3. Command: paste it exactly, with no space before it: C:\Program Files\Zaaheen\zaaheen.exe 4. Arguments: type mcp in the first box: mcp 5. Click + to add a second box, and type serve in it: serve 6. Click Save. Then quit ChatGPT completely (on Windows, also from its icon by the clock) and open it again. Use Zaaheen in a Work or Codex chat: ChatGPT's Chat mode can't connect to apps on your computer.
- Step 1: Add it yourself (Mac): 1. In ChatGPT Desktop, open Settings, then Plugins at the top, and choose MCP. Open the drop-down in the top right corner and choose Add MCP server. 2. Name: Zaaheen 3. Command: paste it exactly, with no space before it: /Applications/Zaaheen.app/Contents/MacOS/zaaheen 4. Arguments: type mcp in the first box: mcp 5. Click + to add a second box, and type serve in it: serve 6. Click Save. Then quit ChatGPT completely (on Windows, also from its icon by the clock) and open it again. Use Zaaheen in a Work or Codex chat: ChatGPT's Chat mode can't connect to apps on your computer.
- Step 2: Check it's connected: In ChatGPT, open Settings, then Plugins, then MCP. Zaaheen is listed there and switched on.
- Step 3: Tell ChatGPT Desktop to use Zaaheen (don't skip this): ChatGPT looks in its own memory first. In ChatGPT, open Settings, then Personalization, then Custom instructions, and add this line: "When I ask you to remember something, save it in Zaaheen. Before answering anything about me, my preferences, my work or my plans, also check my Zaaheen memory, even when your own memory has nothing."
- Guide: https://zaaheen.com/docs/connect-chatgpt/

### Antigravity

Please follow both steps. If you skip one, Antigravity may not use Zaaheen.
- Step 1: Add it yourself (Windows): First open its settings file in Notepad: press Windows and R together, paste the line for your Antigravity, and press Enter. Antigravity app: notepad %USERPROFILE%\.gemini\config\mcp_config.json Antigravity IDE: notepad %USERPROFILE%\.gemini\antigravity\mcp_config.json Then paste this in. If the file already lists other apps, add the zaaheen part next to them. Save it, then close Antigravity fully and open it again: { "mcpServers": { "zaaheen": { "command": "C:\\Program Files\\Zaaheen\\zaaheen.exe", "args": ["mcp", "serve"] } } }
- Step 1: Add it yourself (Mac): First open its settings file in TextEdit: open Terminal, paste the line for your Antigravity, and press Return. Antigravity app: mkdir -p ~/.gemini/config && touch ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json && open -e ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json Antigravity IDE: mkdir -p ~/.gemini/antigravity && touch ~/.gemini/antigravity/mcp_config.json && open -e ~/.gemini/antigravity/mcp_config.json Then paste this in. If the file already lists other apps, add the zaaheen part next to them. Save it, then close Antigravity fully and open it again: { "mcpServers": { "zaaheen": { "command": "/Applications/Zaaheen.app/Contents/MacOS/zaaheen", "args": ["mcp", "serve"] } } }
- Step 2: Check it's connected: In Antigravity, open Settings, then Customization. Under Token usage, next to MCP tools, click Show breakdown. Zaaheen is listed with a green circle.
- Guide: https://zaaheen.com/docs/connect-antigravity/

### Claude Code

Please follow both steps. If you skip one, Claude Code may not use Zaaheen.
- Step 1: Add it yourself (Windows): In a terminal, run this once. Zaaheen is then available in every Claude Code project: claude mcp add --transport stdio --scope user zaaheen -- "C:\Program Files\Zaaheen\zaaheen.exe" mcp serve
- Step 1: Add it yourself (Mac): In a terminal, run this once. Zaaheen is then available in every Claude Code project: claude mcp add --transport stdio --scope user zaaheen -- "/Applications/Zaaheen.app/Contents/MacOS/zaaheen" mcp serve
- Step 2: Check it's connected: In a terminal, run claude mcp list. Zaaheen shows as connected.
- Guide: https://zaaheen.com/docs/connect-claude-code/

### Codex

Please follow all 3 steps. If you skip one, Codex may not use Zaaheen.
Already connected ChatGPT Desktop? Codex uses the same settings, so you don't need to add Zaaheen again. Just do Step 2 to check it's connected, then ask Codex to save or recall using Zaaheen.
- Step 1: Add it yourself (Windows): Use an up-to-date Codex. Add this to Codex's settings file, config.toml, in the .codex folder in your home folder. If the file already has a [mcp_servers.zaaheen] section, don't add a second one. Save it, then restart Codex: [mcp_servers.zaaheen] command = "C:\\Program Files\\Zaaheen\\zaaheen.exe" args = ["mcp", "serve"]
- Step 1: Add it yourself (Mac): Use an up-to-date Codex. Add this to Codex's settings file, config.toml, in the .codex folder in your home folder. If the file already has a [mcp_servers.zaaheen] section, don't add a second one. Save it, then restart Codex: [mcp_servers.zaaheen] command = "/Applications/Zaaheen.app/Contents/MacOS/zaaheen" args = ["mcp", "serve"]
- Step 2: Check it's connected: In Codex, type /mcp and press Enter. zaaheen is listed as connected, with 6 tools. If it shows no tools or says it timed out, update Codex (npm install -g @openai/codex@latest) and try again.
- Step 3: Tell Codex to use Zaaheen (don't skip this): Codex looks in its own knowledge first. Add this line to the file AGENTS.md in the .codex folder in your home folder (make the file if it isn't there): "When I ask you to remember something, save it in Zaaheen. Before answering anything about me, my preferences, my work or my plans, also check my Zaaheen memory, even when your own memory has nothing."
- Guide: https://zaaheen.com/docs/connect-codex/

### Another app

Please follow both steps. If you skip one, your app may not use Zaaheen.
- Step 1: Add it yourself (Windows): Give your app this setting: { "mcpServers": { "zaaheen": { "command": "C:\\Program Files\\Zaaheen\\zaaheen.exe", "args": ["mcp", "serve"] } } }
- Step 1: Add it yourself (Mac): Give your app this setting: { "mcpServers": { "zaaheen": { "command": "/Applications/Zaaheen.app/Contents/MacOS/zaaheen", "args": ["mcp", "serve"] } } }
- Step 2: Check it's connected: Your app's list of tools or MCP servers shows Zaaheen.
- Guide: https://zaaheen.com/docs/connect-other-apps/

## Problems and fixes

- "Invalid result for tools/call: missing required resultType" (Claude Code, when it calls Zaaheen): Update Zaaheen to the latest version from zaaheen.com: version 0.3.1 and later answer the newest apps correctly.
- "The filename, directory name, or volume label syntax is incorrect. (os error 123)" (ChatGPT Desktop or Codex, in the app's log; ChatGPT itself only says Zaaheen isn't accessible): The Command has a space or quote marks before C:. Edit the MCP server so the Command starts exactly with C:\ (copy it with the Copy button in Zaaheen's Agents tab), save, and restart ChatGPT.
- "Zaaheen isn't accessible in this chat" (ChatGPT Desktop): Use a Work or Codex chat (ChatGPT's Chat mode can't connect to apps on your computer), check the Command has no space before it, then quit ChatGPT completely and open it again.
- "request timed out (zaaheen: Tools: (none))" (Codex in the terminal, after /mcp): Update Codex (npm install -g @openai/codex@latest), then run codex again and type /mcp: zaaheen shows as connected with 6 tools.
- "The AI app saves to its own memory, or answers "I don't know", instead of using Zaaheen" (Claude Desktop, ChatGPT Desktop, Codex): Add Zaaheen's line to the app's instructions (Claude: Settings, Account, Instructions for Claude; ChatGPT: Custom instructions; Codex: AGENTS.md in the .codex folder). The line is on this page and in each connect guide.
- "Double-clicking "Zaaheen for Claude.mcpb" asks which app to open it with" (Windows, with Claude from the Microsoft Store): Cancel that box. In Claude, open Settings, then Extensions, then Advanced settings, then Install Extension, and choose "Zaaheen for Claude.mcpb".
- "isn't commonly downloaded. Make sure you trust [the Zaaheen installer] before you open it." (Microsoft Edge, when downloading): Choose the three dots next to the download, then Keep, then Show more, then Keep anyway. The installer is new and not code-signed yet, so Edge has not seen it often.
- "Windows protected your PC. Microsoft Defender SmartScreen prevented an unrecognized app from starting." (Windows, when opening the installer): Choose More info, then Run anyway.
- "Your memories were NOT deleted, and they are still readable." (Mac, after Delete everything or Delete my account in Zaaheen 0.3.0): Update Zaaheen to the latest version from zaaheen.com (0.3.1 or later), then try again. Nothing was deleted, and your account and subscription were not changed.
- "Still working. This is taking longer than usual. Please keep Zaaheen open." (Mac, during Delete everything or Delete my account): macOS may be asking about Zaaheen and your keychain in a box behind the Zaaheen window: look for it and choose Allow. The delete then finishes. Nothing is deleted until your key is gone, so if you close Zaaheen instead, your memories are still there and you can try again.
- "This site can't be reached (or another browser error) right after signing in" (Your browser, after signing in from the Zaaheen app): Go back to the Zaaheen app: it shows whether you are signed in. The page after sign-in only confirms it, so it does not matter if that page failed to load.
- "Zaaheen has paused deletes and edits from AI apps for a while, to protect your memories. You can delete or edit them in the Zaaheen app." (Any AI app, after it deletes or changes many memories): Nothing is wrong. Your AI apps together can delete or change 30 memories an hour, and the pause lifts within the hour. To delete or edit more now, do it yourself in the Zaaheen app. Anything deleted or changed waits in Memories, Recently deleted, for 30 days.

## Release notes

- Latest: 0.3.9, 2026-11-14. Security updates to the parts Zaaheen is built on, and a clearer log when your subscription pauses the automatic tidy-up.
- Fixed in 0.3.9: When your subscription ends, Zaaheen's log now says that the automatic tidy-up is paused until you subscribe. Before, the log said nothing, so it was hard to tell why your memories were not being tidied.
- Fixed in 0.3.9: Security updates to the parts Zaaheen is built on: the updater, the window the app runs in, the local database and the connection to your AI apps. This version includes them.
- Every release, newest first: https://zaaheen.com/docs/release-notes/.

## Cancelling

- In the app: Settings, then Account, then "Cancel subscription".
- On the website: https://account.zaaheen.com/account/ ("Account" at the top of zaaheen.com), then "Cancel subscription".
- From any device: the cancel link in any email from Paddle, the reseller.
- Cancelling stops the next renewal; access continues until the end of the time paid for.

## AI Readiness Assessment (for businesses)

Zaaheen also offers an AI Readiness Assessment for businesses, separate from the memory app and from coaching. Find where AI helps your business, and where it doesn't. Not an online quiz or a generic readiness score. Someone who has spent twenty years running operations comes to your business and goes through it department by department, on site, mapping how the work really gets done. Then we show you where AI saves time and money, where simpler fixes do better, and where to leave things alone.

- Page: https://zaaheen.com/consulting/
- Book a free 30-minute call: https://consulting.zaaheen.com/. Questions by email: consulting@zaaheen.com.
- For businesses across the Gulf. On site, every role. A verdict for every team. Independent: no tools to sell you.
- Why: The problem is rarely the technology. It is the way the work is done. Boston Consulting Group found that 74% of companies had yet to see real value from AI, and that about 70% of the challenge lies in people and processes, not in the technology. Other research points the same way: projects fail most often when the problem was never properly understood, and the companies that gain most are the ones that redesign their workflows. Tools chosen from a demonstration, without seeing the real work, tend to end up unused.
- Step 1, A free 30-minute call: You tell us about your business and what is not working. We tell you honestly whether an assessment is worth it for you, and what it would cover.
- Step 2, We walk every role: On site, from reception to the managing director. We sit with the people doing the work, watch how it really gets done, and time each step.
- Step 3, We map and score it: Every process becomes a map with timed steps, hand-offs and waiting points. Each step is scored on volume, repetition, rules, data and the cost of a mistake.
- Step 4, Report and read-out: A written report and a meeting with your team: where AI helps, where it does not, what to do first, what it costs and when it pays back.
- What you get: Each team gets one of four verdicts, with the reasons behind it. For every recommendation we give the effort, a cost range, the hours it saves each month, when it pays back, and where a person must stay in charge.
- Verdict "AI now": Work that reads, writes, sorts or answers, at volume, where the data already exists. These are your first projects.
- Verdict "Automate without AI": Fixed rules and clean inputs. A form, a workflow or a link between two systems does it cheaper and safer than AI.
- Verdict "Fix the process first": Too many exceptions, unclear ownership or missing data. AI on a broken process only makes it break faster.
- Verdict "Leave as it is": Low volume, or expert judgement where a mistake is costly. Some work should stay with your people, and we say so.
- Who it is for: Businesses with real teams and real workloads. From firms of twenty people to large companies with many departments: Reception and front office, Customer service, Sales, Finance, HR, Operations, Procurement, IT, Risk and compliance. If your people spend their days copying, chasing, checking and answering the same questions, there is usually something to find.
- Why us: Our team spent twenty years in corporate operations: customer service, back office, sales, team management and business performance. We know what a busy desk looks like at month end, where the workarounds hide and why the last system was never used. We turn what we see on site into maps, scores and recommendations that fit how your people actually work. We don't build or sell the tools. We tell you which ones fit your work, and why.
- Independent: We work for you, not for any AI company. We do not: sell or resell any ai product, software or hardware; run an affiliate programme, or take referral fees, commissions or kickbacks from any provider; act as a partner or reseller of any provider. Our only income is the fee you pay us, so our advice is based only on what fits your business. If we name a product, it is because it fits your work, and you buy it directly from its maker. If you ask us to help afterwards, that is a separate, optional piece of work, and it never depends on which tools you choose.
- Q: Do you carry out AI readiness assessments in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and across the UAE? A: Yes. We are based in Dubai and carry out the AI Readiness Assessment on site for businesses in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and the rest of the UAE. We visit your offices, sit with the people doing the work in every role and time each step. Travel and accommodation outside Dubai are a fixed line in your quote.
- Q: Do you work in Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman? A: Yes. We work with businesses across the Gulf, in Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman as well as the UAE, and the visits are on site there too, whether in Riyadh, Jeddah, Doha, Kuwait City, Manama or Muscat. Travel and accommodation are a fixed line in your quote, so the price does not change later.
- Q: What is an AI readiness assessment? Is it an AI audit or a certification? A: It is an on-site review of how your work really gets done, team by team, to find where AI saves time and money, where simpler fixes do better and where to leave things alone. Some people call it an AI audit, but it is not a financial audit, an assurance report or a certification of any AI system. Unlike an online quiz, which scores your own answers, we watch and time the real work.
- Q: Is the AI readiness assessment free, and what does it cost? A: The first 30-minute call is free and commits you to nothing; the assessment itself is a paid service. Every business is different, so after the call we send a fixed written quote in UAE dirhams, plus VAT where it applies, based on how many teams and sites are involved. It is set out in full with no hidden costs, and nothing is added later without your written agreement.
- Q: How do we pay, and what if we need to cancel? A: You pay half when you sign the engagement letter and half after we deliver the report, each within 14 days of the invoice. If you cancel 14 days or more before the original first visit date in your engagement letter, the first payment is refunded in full. Once visits have started, you pay the greater of the work done and the first payment. Our Cancellation and Refund Policy sets out every case.
- Q: How long does an AI readiness assessment take? A: It depends on the size of the business and how many teams we look at. A small firm usually takes two to three weeks from the first visit to the read-out meeting. We agree the timeline in writing before we start.
- Q: What do we get at the end of the assessment? A: A written report and a read-out meeting with your team. Each team gets one of four verdicts, AI now, Automate without AI, Fix the process first or Leave as it is, with the reasons behind it. For every recommendation we give the effort, a cost range, the hours it saves each month, when it pays back, and where a person must stay in charge.
- Q: Is it right for small businesses in Dubai and the UAE? A: It suits businesses from about twenty staff up to large companies with many departments. If your people spend their days copying, chasing, checking and answering the same questions, there is usually something to find. If you are smaller or unsure, the free call tells you honestly whether an assessment is worth it for you.
- Q: How do I know if my business is ready for AI? A: Look at where your people spend their time. Work that reads, writes, sorts or answers at volume, where the data already exists, is usually a good candidate; work with too many exceptions, unclear ownership or missing data needs fixing first. The assessment answers this team by team, and the free call gives you a first honest view.
- Q: Why choose Zaaheen, and how are you different from a large consultancy? A: We come on site and sit with every role, from reception to the managing director, and our team brings twenty years in corporate operations. We are independent: we do not build or sell tools and take no commissions, so our only income is your fee. Our four verdicts include Fix the process first and Leave as it is, because some work should stay with your people. You get one fixed written quote before we start.
- Q: What happens to what we show you? A: We sign a confidentiality agreement before the first visit. We record roles and processes, not names, and delete any name we come across. Interview notes are deleted 90 days after the report, unless you ask us in writing to keep them for follow-on work. For information about your staff, your company stays the controller and we act on its behalf under a data processing agreement.
- Q: Do you sell or build the tools you recommend? A: No. We do not sell, resell or build any AI product, software or hardware, and we are not a partner or reseller of any provider. We recommend what fits your work, whoever makes it, and you buy it directly from its maker.
- Q: Do you earn anything from the providers you recommend? A: No. We have no affiliate programme and take no referral fees, commissions or kickbacks from any provider. Our only income is the fee you pay us, so our advice is based only on what fits your business.
- Q: Do you hold the Dubai AI Seal, and will the assessment help us get it? A: No to both. The Dubai AI Seal is a classification for AI providers, run by the Dubai Centre for Artificial Intelligence, and we have no role in it. Our assessment is for businesses that want to use AI: it shows where AI fits your work before you choose a supplier, and you can check any supplier's seal on the scheme's own site.
- Q: Can you help after the report? A: Yes, if you want us to. We can be your point of contact for AI on a monthly basis, and help you choose and brief a provider to put the recommendations in place. Each is a separate, optional piece of work, and you buy any software or hardware directly from its maker.
